text:
### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, every one of the 200 cases contained A25, A26, A27, A28, A31, A36, A37 and A42. In the later window, A27 appears in about 54 in 100 cases (107 of 200) and A36, A37 and A42 in about 47 in 100 each (94–95 of 200); their mean occurrences per trace halve from about 1.0 to about 0.5. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004]
- In the later window, A27 and the three activities A36/A37/A42 are close to mutually exclusive: they co-occur in only about 1–2 of 200 cases, whereas they co-occurred in every case before. A25, A26, A28 and A31 still appear in every case in both windows. [REL011, REL012, REL013, POS001, POS002, POS004, POS005]
- The placement of A36/A37/A42 flipped relative to A26 and A28: before, A36 ran before A26 in 100 of 100 cases and before A28 in about 199 of 200; in the later window, A26 and A28 precede them in about 95 of 100 cases where both occur, and the activity following the trio changed from A28 to A31. [REL006, REL007, REL008, REL014, REL015, REL016, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]
- Positions shifted accordingly: the trio's median relative position moved from about 0.40 to about 0.58 of the trace, A28 moved earlier (mean 0.46 to 0.39) and A26 slightly earlier (0.60 to 0.54). [POS006, POS007, POS008, POS004, POS002]
- Routing changed at A25 and A26: A25's outgoing transitions led to A36/A37/A42 in about 96 of 100 cases before and to A28 in about 97 of 100 in the later window; A26 led to A27 in 99 of 100 before, and in the later window leads to A27 in about 52 of 100 and to one of A36/A37/A42 in about 44 of 100. [DIR001, DIR002]
- Distances changed accordingly: A25 is followed by A28 within one step in about 97 of 100 later cases (previously the gap was always 4–5 steps), and the A26-to-A31 distance is 2 steps in A27-cases but about 4 steps in trio-cases (about 53 versus 43 in 100). [LAG001, LAG005]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

- The evidence supports the possibility that A36/A37/A42 were repositioned and turned into an alternative to A27. In the earlier window, cases ran A25, then the trio in mixed internal order, then A28, A26 and A27, then A31; in the later window, cases run A25, A28, A26 and then either A27 (about 53 in 100) or the trio (about 47 in 100), followed by A31, with the trio's internal order still mixed. [DIR001, REL014, REL005, LAG001, LAG005, DIR002, REL011, REL020, POS004, POS002]
- This is shown directly by relational and positional evidence: the order flips between the trio and A26/A28, the trio's later median position, the successor changes at A25 and A26, the collapse of the A25-to-A28 distance from 4–5 steps to 1, and the near-perfect exclusivity between A27 and the trio (about 1–2 co-occurrences in 200 cases versus every case before). With 48 qualifying items against roughly 0.73 expected for an unchanged process, chance cannot explain the evidence as a whole, though most items express one coherent shift rather than independent confirmations. [REL006, REL007, REL008, REL014, REL015, REL016, POS006, POS007, POS008, DIR001, DIR002, LAG001, REL011, REL012, REL013]
- Limitations: the comparison shows how behaviour differs between the two samples but cannot establish how the change came about; in particular, it cannot rule out that the later window reflects a different mix of process variants rather than one modified flow, although the earlier window's full participation in all eight activities makes a pre-existing hidden variant unlikely. A few lag items about the trio's new internal distances rest on only 1–2 observations and were not relied upon. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, LAG002, LAG003, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008]
